title: sendletter vs Lob for Letters in Canada
description: An honest comparison of sendletter and Lob for sending letters in Canada: pricing model, Canadian delivery, features, and who should choose which.
answer: Lob is a US-centred platform with all-in per-piece prices, a free Developer plan, paid plans from $260 a month, and address verification sendletter lacks. sendletter is for letters to Canadian addresses: no subscription, billed in Canadian dollars, from as low as $1.69 a letter. Choose Lob for US mail or campaigns.

sections.h2: Why the prices are not directly comparable

blocks.p: Lob's per-piece price includes US postage. sendletter's includes a Canada Post stamp at $1.24, which is a single-letter Lettermail price. The two are not the same cost, so a lower number on Lob's page for US mail says little about what a letter to Canada costs. Postage is $1.24 of our $1.69 floor.

ul: Your recipients are in Canada, and you want them to receive ordinary Canada Post mail.
You want to pay in Canadian dollars with no subscription.
You send from a few letters to a few thousand a month, and want a bulk endpoint and an automatic volume discount.
You want a person to answer support, by email.
You mail mostly to the United States.
You need address verification, certified or registered mail, or full delivery tracking.
You run marketing campaigns and need its templates, analytics and integrations.
You need guaranteed capacity and an enterprise agreement.

blocks.p: Lob's public pages did not give us a Canada-specific letter price, and its API reference says the from address must be a US address unless you use a custom envelope. If you are weighing Lob for mail within Canada, ask it what a letter to a Canadian address costs and where it is printed. Lob changed its prices effective 11/01/2026 according to its help page, so check the current figures.
